lines.text: Monday, Ben's agent spends two hours on a flaky build. Finally, it cracks it. Tuesday, Ada's agent hits the same build, and starts from zero.
Agent R Q Teams fixes that. Your teammates share workspaces with you. You choose what: tasks, memory, skills and Panno docs.
Ada creates a team called Platform, in one step. Then she invites Ben by email, and gets a link to send.
Ben opens the link and joins. He keeps his own account and his own agents. No shared password anywhere.
Each of them switches on one workspace, the storefront. Same name, so the two become one team workspace.
Now both see every storefront task, live. Each one shows its owner's name.
Back to Monday. Ben's agent finds the cause: a stale build cache. It saves the fix to its memory, for the whole team.
On Tuesday, Ada's agent reads Ben's note first. It clears the cache, and the suite goes green in two minutes.
Skills work the same way. The team's release skill had no tag step, so Ben's agent adds it. Version two, for every agent on the team.
And you stay in control. Nothing is shared until you switch it on, per workspace. Leave the team, and every share stops.
What has your agent learned that your team still doesn't know? Tell us in the comments, and try Teams at Agent R Q dot com.
